hi

") as render, \ mock.patch.object(email, "send", return_value="msg_1"): assert email.send_receipt("inv_1", "a@example.com", 1200) == "msg_1" render.assert_called_once_with("receipt", invoice_id="inv_1", total_minor=1200) def test_send_receipt_is_skipped_when_flag_off(monkeypatch): monkeypatch.delenv("NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_EMAIL", raising=False) with mock.patch.object(email, "render") as render, \ mock.patch.object(email, "send") as send: assert email.send_receipt("inv_1", "a@example.com", 1200) is None render.assert_not_called() send.assert_not_called() EOF python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib tests 2>&1 | tail -5" }

`send_receipt` in `services/notifier/notifier/email.py` is now behind a feature flag, and both notifier tests pass. I read "the new receipt email" as `send_receipt`, since there is no separate new receipt code or template in the repo. Tell me if you meant something else.

- **Flag:** it follows the notifier convention, `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_EMAIL`. The root `flags.toml` and `flags.is_on()` don't apply because the notifier is deployed separately. The email is on only when the variable is exactly `"1"`.
- **Off by default:** when the flag is off, `send_receipt` returns `None` without rendering or sending anything. The one thing to check on your side is whether any caller relies on a message id coming back.
- **Gradual rollout:** this is a single on/off switch per deployment. If you want a percentage rollout or per-customer targeting, that needs more logic. Say if you want it.
- **Tests:** I updated the existing receipt test to set the flag and added one that checks nothing is rendered or sent when it's off. I ran them from `services/notifier` with `python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib tests`.
